experiments.result: in a matched pair on the host's own mini case, an auxiliary term changes the encoder gradient by 1.66e-05 before the host's post-backward assembly and by exactly 0.0 after it
experiments.verdict: the host OVERWRITES the encoder gradient with g_base + w_b/valid_levels * (g'_L1 + g_L2 + g_L3) and never touches the decoder or the codebook gradient, so an auxiliary term that reaches only the encoder is discarded in production however healthy it looks in isolation; only a term that delivers gradient to the codebook can change the exported SIDs

predictions.measurement: a matched pair on the host's mini case: the encoder gradient with and without the term, before and after the host's own projection

explanations.statement: the host overwrites the encoder gradient after the backward, so an auxiliary term that reaches only the encoder is discarded in production, however healthy it looks in isolation

hypotheses.notes: measured on the host's own code path: the encoder gradient difference is 1.66e-05 before the host's post-backward assembly and exactly 0.0 after it, so the two inert arms' training was bit-identical to the control's. A mechanism that wants to move the exported SIDs has to deliver its gradient to the codebook, which the host never overwrites
hypotheses.observation: two arms' trained models are byte-identical to the matched control's, although their mechanisms pass the independent gradient checks

experiments.result: the delivered codebook gradient scales exactly linearly with the mechanism's weight (0.01 -> 2.961e-02, 0.001 -> 2.961e-03, 0.0001 -> 2.961e-04) and the hard assignment's churn is ZERO at every weight, including the production one
experiments.verdict: E1 is NOT supported: the gradient's magnitude scales, but it does not flip the assignment, so magnitude alone does not explain the collapse

experiments.verdict: E2 is REFUTED: the collapse is not a shrinkage toward the items; the used codewords converged onto each other instead

experiments.verdict: E2' is SUPPORTED: the mechanism's codebook gradient pulled the pair's codewords together until the cells merged, and that is the collapse

does the probe export's paired enrichment ratio predict the cold run's ER?

Across the 19 arms that have both a probe export and a cold export, the probe's paired balance predicts the cold run's balance only weakly (Spearman 0.38 for the level-0 Gini, 0.47 for the number of level-0 codes in use) and the probe's paired enrichment ratio predicts the cold run's ER only weakly (0.51). Gating on that ratio would have wrongly refused an arm whose cold run cleared the gate: directed_assignment_prefix_information has a probe ratio of 0.93 and a cold-run ER of 16.95 against the gate's 16.39.

Over the 13 arms that have both a mechanism module and a measured ER, the arms that cleared the gate average -0.032 and the arms that missed it average -0.048 -- the opposite sign to the hypothesis -- and the rank correlation with the ER is 0.27. The mini case is random vectors in a low dimension, which is not the geometry the merge happens in.

explanations.statement: the pair-level ER and the downstream quality move in OPPOSITE directions, and the cause is code concentration: a behaviour-driven merge of the level-0 codes raises the positive match rate and the same merge removes the distinctions the recommender ranks by. predictions.falsifier: a rigid-motion mechanism whose exported level-0 Gini still rises above the control's, or whose ER does not rise at all

predictions.statement: a mechanism that moves the codebook as a rigid body -- a rotation, a shear, an alignment of the configuration with the behaviour graph -- changes the grouping without pulling two codewords together, and therefore raises the ER without concentrating the codes

explanations.statement: the ER's denominator is a function of the cell SIZES alone and its numerator a function of the GROUPING, so the ER can rise without any cell getting worse. No arm has done this: every arm that raised the ER raised it by pulling a pair's codewords together

predictions.falsifier: a prospective arm whose proxy rank and its downstream outcome agree on every arm of a campaign

On the historical cohort, rebuilt from the seed-42 probe rows only, adding G_H1 to the ER lowers the Recall@10 out-of-fold MAE from 0.003753 to 0.002835 and adding D2 lowers it to 0.003169, but both family-cluster confidence intervals span zero, the proxies alone are WORSE than the ER alone, and 17 to 19 of the 38 models are counterexamples where the proxy predicts worse

hypotheses.observation: the mission is one genuinely new mechanism that clears THREE frozen thresholds at once: the frozen Stage-2 Hard-L1 ER above 16.38953942232631, the Stage-3 Recall@10 above 0.06406796775709883 and the Stage-3 NDCG@10 above 0.03530651701940677, against the immutable archived r8_control (ER 16.334505666275888, Recall@10 0.06406796775709883, NDCG@10 0.03530651701940677). predictions.falsifier: a rigid-motion arm that keeps the balance and still does not raise the ER above the control's 16.3345, across several directions

explanations.statement: a rigid motion changes which items are grouped without changing how the cells are sized, so it is the right instrument for the requirement the measurements state; this arm's balance confirms it, and its ER says only that this particular direction of the motion did not raise the pair-level enrichment

predictions.falsifier: such an arm still loses Recall@10 and NDCG@10 against the archived control
predictions.measurement: the one Stage-3 each of those arms is allowed, against the archived control's 0.06406796775709883 and 0.03530651701940677

explanations.statement: the arms that clear the gate and keep the balance are the population the mission is about, and their downstream quality has never been measured: the arm with the best ER of the whole campaign (17.2983, level-0 Gini 0.229, 255 codes in use, 63.8 branches) and an arm at 16.6019 whose balance is better than the control's (Gini 0.193, 244 codes, 66.5 branches) had no Stage-3 at all

hypotheses.notes: the controller now adopts any arm the store knows that cleared the gate and has no Stage-3, so an arm is never left unmeasured because a round moved on
hypotheses.observation: the rigid-motion family does what it was designed to do, and that is new evidence. The first arm that moved the codebook as a rigid body kept its balance: 239 level-0 codes in use against the control's 245, a level-0 Gini of 0.203 against the control's 0.216, and 67.2 prefix branches against 65.9. Its ER, however, FELL: 16.2266 against the control's 16.3345 and below the gate. So the balance and the enrichment ratio can be decoupled -- a mechanism can keep the codes balanced -- and the missing ingredient in this family is the DIRECTION of the motion, not its rigidity.

predictions.falsifier: an arm that clears the gate with a level-0 Gini at or below the control's and still loses more than 0.0005 of Recall@10
predictions.measurement: the one Stage-3 each arm is allowed, against the archived control
predictions.statement: among the arms that clear the gate, the one whose balance is closest to the control's loses the least downstream quality, and one that keeps the balance exactly would lose nothing

explanations.statement: the loss of the downstream quality comes from the CONCENTRATION, and the concentration is what the enrichment ratio pays for. An arm can therefore clear the gate and keep the balance, and the question is whether the pair-level enrichment can be raised by a partition that does not concentrate

predictions.falsifier: an arm with no measurable balance change and a raised ER that still loses downstream quality
predictions.measurement: the level-0 Gini, the number of codes in use, the prefix branches and the Stage-3 result of every arm
predictions.statement: if the mechanism term itself is what costs the downstream quality, then the arms with the smallest balance change lose the least, and an arm with NO balance change and a raised ER would lose nothing at all

explanations.statement: an alternative reading: every arm is slightly worse than the control because the mechanism term perturbs the quantisation whatever it does, and the concentration only adds to that. The two readings are distinguished by an arm that keeps the balance exactly

hypotheses.next_experiment: read the four pending downstream measurements of the arms that cleared the gate, and let the next portfolio target the arms whose balance change is smallest while the ER rises
hypotheses.notes: the pending measurements are the sharpest test yet: one of them has a better balance than the control and an ER above the gate, so if the hypothesis holds it is the arm that loses the least
hypotheses.observation: the downstream loss is concentrated in the arms that lost their balance, not in the arms that raised the ER. Grouping the measured arms by whether the export kept the control's level-0 Gini and its prefix branches: the arms that kept them lose on average 0.000165 of Recall@10 and 0.000319 of NDCG@10, and the arms that lost them lose on average 0.001928 and 0.001355, an order of magnitude more. The arm with the best ER of the whole campaign (17.2983) and the arm whose balance is BETTER than the control's (Gini 0.193 against 0.216, 66.5 branches against 65.9) had no downstream measurement at all and are being measured now. This is a description of ten arms, not a causal claim.

predictions.falsifier: an arm that holds both numbers and still loses more than 0.0005 of Recall@10

predictions.statement: an arm that raises the ER while the largest level-0 cell stays at or below the control's 237 items and the L1 -> L2 tree keeps at least 65.9 branches per code will lose less downstream quality than an arm that does not

explanations.statement: what the recommender loses is the TAIL of the level-0 usage and the width of the prefix tree, not the evenness of the usage: a few very large cells and a narrow tree are what a beam search cannot walk, while a slightly uneven distribution of many small cells costs it nothing

predictions.falsifier: neither signal separates the arms across a further campaign of the same size
predictions.measurement: the D2 and the G_H1 of every arm against its Stage-3 result, case by case

explanations.statement: an alternative reading: the eleven arms are too few and the correlations are too weak to select a target, and what really matters is the mechanism's own effect on the training -- the decoder, the quantisation error, the gradient the host discards -- which the export's shape cannot show

hypotheses.next_experiment: aim the next portfolios at the largest level-0 cell and the branch count rather than at the Gini, and use the conditional L2 discrimination and the history-conditioned gain to say WHY an arm loses what it loses

hypotheses.observation: the account of what costs the downstream quality is WRONG as it stood, and the correction is measured. The arm with the second-best ER of the campaign (17.2983) has a structure almost identical to the control's -- 255 level-0 codes against 245, a Gini of 0.229 against 0.216, the same sequence information (0.1045 against 0.1044) -- and it lost MORE downstream quality than any other arm in the cohort, 0.0039 of Recall@10. Over the eleven arms that carry both measurements, the Gini's rank correlation with the downstream loss is -0.07, which is no correlation, while the TAIL of the level-0 usage, the largest cell, gives -0.52 and the width of the L1 -> L2 prefix tree gives +0.44. The requirement the campaign had been aiming at was therefore aimed at the wrong statistic.

predictions.measurement: the G_H1 and the D2 of every arm against its Stage-3 result, case by case
predictions.statement: the history-conditioned gain and the conditional level-2 discrimination separate the arms that lose downstream quality from the ones that do not, where the export's shape does not

explanations.statement: the export's shape is a SUMMARY, and the thing that costs the recommender is the mechanism's effect on the training, which the summary cannot show: the codes can look like the control's and still carry a loss, and the arm that looked most like the control did lose the most

predictions.falsifier: an arm whose conditional set is large enough to support a decision, measured on the same frozen pairs
predictions.measurement: the conditional set's size and its support flags, per arm
predictions.statement: the D2's positive conditional set stays a few hundred pairs for every arm, so the D2 is a diagnostic and not a ranking signal

explanations.statement: the conditional level-2 discrimination cannot be rescued on the frozen pairs, because the conditioning is too rare there; it is a property of the pair set and not of the mechanism

hypotheses.next_experiment: let the cohort grow: every arm measured from now carries the ER, the conditional L2 discrimination, the history-conditioned gain and, when it clears the gate, the one Stage-3, and the question the cohort has to answer is which of those separates the arms that lose from the ones that do not
hypotheses.notes: the brief now says plainly that the balance is a requirement rather than a mechanism, that the D2 is weakly supported, and that the history gain is neutral so far -- so the agent is not asked to believe more than was measured
hypotheses.observation: the two limits of the current instruments, both measured. FIRST: the balance measures are only moderately associated with the downstream loss -- the largest level-0 cell gives -0.52 and the prefix tree +0.44 over a dozen arms, and an arm that holds both can still lose, so the requirement is a constraint rather than a mechanism. SECOND: the conditional level-2 discrimination is intrinsically weakly supported on the frozen behaviour pairs, where only about one per cent of the pairs share their level-1 code: the positive conditional set is a few hundred pairs, and every arm's D2 so far carries a low-support flag. The history-conditioned gain is the more promising of the two signals and it is neutral so far: the rigid arm that kept its balance reads 0.1232 and the repartition arm 0.1234, against a historical range of 0.004 to 0.195.

predictions.falsifier: an arm with a history-conditioned gain in the top of the cohort's band and an ER above the gate that still loses more than 0.0005 of Recall@10
predictions.measurement: the G_H1 and the ER of every arm against its one Stage-3, case by case
predictions.statement: a mechanism that raises the frozen ER while also raising the history-conditioned gain will lose less downstream quality than one that raises the ER alone

explanations.statement: the codes' history-conditioned predictability is the property the recommender actually consumes: a pair-level enrichment ratio that rises without the codes carrying more history gives the recommender nothing to predict from, whatever the ratio says

predictions.falsifier: a cohort in which the cell and the tree predict the loss at least as well as the history gain does
predictions.measurement: the rank correlation of each structural measure and of the gain with the downstream Recall@10, over the same arms
predictions.statement: the largest level-0 cell and the prefix tree do not explain the downstream loss either, once the history gain is in the picture

explanations.statement: the balance hypothesis is REFUTED by the sharpest test: the arm with the best balance of the whole cohort -- ER 16.6019 with a level-0 Gini of 0.193 against the control's 0.216, a largest cell of 253 against 237 and 66.5 prefix branches against 65.9, better on all three -- lost the most downstream quality of any arm, 0.0108 of Recall@10, three times the next worst. Holding the balance is not what protects the recommender

hypotheses.next_experiment: a portfolio that aims at the history-conditioned gain as well as the frozen ER, and a cohort that repeats this comparison prospectively, because this one is retrospective and the arms were inspected as they came
hypotheses.notes: the brief now says which instrument the measurements point at, and says what the measurements do not establish: a moderate association over twelve arms, not a mechanism and not a certification
hypotheses.observation: the campaign's own cohort says which instrument is worth anything. Every arm that had an export was given its one history-conditioned probe, so twelve arms now carry the frozen ER, the history-conditioned gain and the one Stage-3 each of them is allowed. Across those twelve, the history-conditioned gain's rank correlation with the downstream Recall@10 is +0.45 and with the NDCG@10 +0.44, while the frozen ER's is +0.10 and +0.15. The gain's range across the cohort is narrow -- 0.1201 to 0.1258 -- and the ordering inside that band is what tracks the loss. This is a retrospective association on a cohort that has already been inspected, not a causal claim and not a certification.
